title: A Novel Method for Reservoir Outflow Simulation Based on Spearman Rank Correlation Between Satellite‐Derived Water Elevations and Model‐Simulated Reservoir Storage
content:
Abstract

Accurate simulation of reservoir outflow is essential for integrated water resource management. However, the limited availability of operational data for reservoirs often hinder the accuracy of outflow simulations. Satellite remote sensing, combined with water balance approaches, provides an effective solution for calculating outflows. However, these methods are typically retrospective during the historical satellite observation period, making them less applicable for future simulations and forecasts. In this study, we propose a calibration scheme for the Reservoir Outflow Model (ROM) to reconstruct outflows by calculating the Spearman rank correlation (rs ${r}_{s}$) between satellite-derived surface water elevations (SWE) and ROM-simulated storage. We test the applicability of rs ${r}_{s}$ across four ROMs applied to nine reservoirs in China and compare it with a calibration scheme using gauged outflow data. Additionally, we compare the proposed scheme with two hybrid methods that combine satellite remote sensing and water balance techniques. Results show that the scheme based on rs ${r}_{s}$ effectively reconstructs the historical outflows of the nine reservoirs (NSE>0.6 $\text{NSE}\, > \,0.6$ and KGE>0.7 $\text{KGE}\, > \,0.7$), with minimal deviation (average ΔNSE ${\Delta }\text{NSE}$ and ΔKGE ${\Delta }\text{KGE}$ less 0.03) compared to the calibration scheme using gauged outflow data. In contrast to the two hybrid methods, the proposed scheme achieves comparable reservoir outflow results with less data (average ΔNSE ${\Delta }\text{NSE}$ and ΔKGE ${\Delta }\text{KGE}$ less 0.07). Our study explores the potential of satellite-derived SWE to drive ROMs for outflow simulation, providing critical support for addressing global water challenges and mitigating the impacts of climate change.
